context:
Goal: the envelope composer is easy to tap and type in on the phone.
Problem (rule): the card name and note fields draw about 48 pt tall, two lines, where the web's are single-line inputs. A one-line field fails Apple's tap-area check, because Cochin 16 is under 20 pt (measured 2026-10-27). The Tally search field has the same shape. The debt closes only on your ruling or a one-line field that passes.
Based on (measured): the 2026-10-27 scratch audit matrix.
Based on (read): OrphanedView.swift:173-174 and 225-226 set two to three lines on purpose.
Departs from: OrphanedView.swift:ComposerView — the web fields are one line; option a keeps two-line fields on the phone.
Meanwhile: the phone ships two-line fields.
home: branch records-owner-1523: ruling filed, debt native-composer-fields-two-lines closed

options.gain: Each field is a big, easy tap target, and the audit passes.
options.how: The fields stay two lines tall, and the debt closes.
options.label: Two lines are right on the phone
options.lose: The fields look taller than the web's.

options.how: A lane tries a one-line field with a taller tap area until one passes.
options.label: Keep looking for a one-line field
options.lose: More test rounds, and none has passed yet.

ref: debt native-composer-fields-two-lines (composer fields draw two lines tall); decision typography-cochin-and-mono
title: The phone's envelope composer fields are two lines tall, where the web's are one. Is that right?
why: It is the only shape that passes the tap-size check today, and a bigger tap target helps on the phone.
